The observations of objectionable conditions and practices listed on the front of this form
are reported:
1. Pursuant to Section 704(b) of the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act, or
2. To assist firms inspected in complying with the Acts and regulations enforced by the
Food and Drug Administration.


Section 704(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 USC 374(b)) provides:
"Upon completion of any such inspection of a factory, warehouse, consulting
laboratory, or other establishment, and prior to leaving the premises, the officer or
employee making the inspection shall give to the owner, operator, or agent in charge a
report in writing setting forth any conditions or practices observed by him which, in his
judgment, indicate that any food, drug, device, or cosmetic in such establishment (1)
consists in whole or in part of any filthy, putrid, or decomposed substance, or (2) has
been prepared, packed, or held under insanitary conditions whereby it may have become
contaminated with filth, or whereby it may have been rendered injurious to health. A copy
of such report shall be sent promptly to the Secretary."

rows.body: In strict Lean manufacturing taxonomy, equipment cleaning is classified as a business non-value-added activity. It does not physically transform the product in a way the patient directly pays for, yet it is non-negotiable for ensuring patient safety, preventing cross-contamination, and maintaining regulatory compliance. Because cleaning sits squarely within equipment changeover downtime, poorly designed cleaning processes and overly rigid validation frameworks act as a direct tax on plant capacity.

ncr_translation_input.outcome: Based on the areas inspected, the people met and the documents reviewed, and considering the findings of the inspection, including the observations listed in the Inspection Report, Cipla Limited, located at Plot D-7, D-22, D-27, MIDC Industrial Area, Kurkumbh Village, Taluka - Daund, Pune, Maharashtra, 413802 (India), was considered to be operating at an acceptable level of compliance with WHO GMP Guidelines. All the non-compliances observed during the inspection that were listed in the full report as well as those reflected in the WHOPIR were addressed by the manufacturer to a satisfactory level prior to the publication of the WHOPIR This WHOPIR will remain valid for 3 years, provided that the outcome of any inspection conducted during this period is positive.
ncr_translation_input.s1: The pharmaceutical quality system (PQS) principles were adequately described in the Quality Manual. A documented system for quality assurance (QA) at the corporate level was established, with procedures covering key quality elements. The quality department, including QA and QC, was separate from the production department. Operations were documented in writing, and critical GMP requirements were essentially met. The procedures reviewed and discussed during the inspection were generally acceptable. The following major computerized systems were used by the site: S. No. …
ncr_translation_input.s10: The SOP for training described the GMP training requirements. The Learning Management System (LMS) was used to schedule, assign, register, execute, evaluate, and record internal and external training activities. Upon review of the data integrity policy, it was noted that personnel did not receive the training before starting their on-site work. The deficiencies raised from this section have been adequately addressed, and their effective implementation will be verified during future PQ inspections.
ncr_translation_input.s11: The procedure for personnel health and hygiene was reviewed and found to be appropriate. All staff working at the site were subject to annual medical examinations, with the exception of visual inspectors who undergo semi-annual eye checks in order to keep them qualified for their work activities. During the visit to the manufacturing areas, hand sanitizers and appropriate gowning were provided.
ncr_translation_input.s12: There were three units (APIs and FPPs) at the Kurkumbh site, whereas Unit-I was relevant and covered during this inspection, as the WHO prequalified product was authorized to be produced at this unit. Facility layouts were made available. In general, premises were constructed, designed, and maintained to suit the operations to be carried out and prevent the risk of contamination of materials and products. Within Unit-I, two blocks (Pharma-I & Pharma-II) manufacture FPPs of different dosage forms. …
ncr_translation_input.s13: Production equipment was of a good standard and appeared to be well-maintained. Spot checks of production balances and differential pressure gauges indicated that equipment and devices were calibrated in a timely manner. The workflow in the facility was appropriately designed, and the equipment appeared to be installed to facilitate production and reduce the risk of contamination and mix-ups. In general, most production equipment was identified by its content or purpose, with cleanliness status identified by appropriate labels. …
ncr_translation_input.s14: The inspector visited the warehouse located on the ground floor of Pharma I. The materials were received at the receiving bay, verified for accuracy, and accepted. A SAP checklist was used to record details of incoming material receipt. Gelatin from Gelita Germany was received on 15/05/2026. The APIs were sampled 100%, whereas excipients were sampled based on √n+1. It was noted that some excipients were sampled at 100% (such as Glycerine, PEG 6000). The sampling was carried out under RLAF, and the area was equipped with separate MAL and PAL. …
ncr_translation_input.s15: Documents were designed, prepared, reviewed, and distributed in accordance with the relevant document control procedure. Documents were approved, signed, and dated, and had unambiguous content. The procedure covered all quality documents except for validation documents, which were governed by a different procedure. Procedures were reviewed regularly. QA was responsible for monitoring the periodic review of procedures. CIPDOX (a document management system) was used to prepare SOPs and specifications. …
ncr_translation_input.s16: Production operations followed clearly defined procedures in accordance with manufacturing and marketing authorizations. Handling of materials and products, including receipt and cleaning, quarantine, sampling, storage, labeling, dispensing, processing, packaging, and distribution, was performed in accordance with written procedures and instructions, and all activities were recorded. Deviations from procedures were recorded and investigated. Checks on yields and reconciliation of quantities were carried out. …
ncr_translation_input.s17: The QC function was independent of other departments. The laboratory was staffed with 96 personnel and equipped with 36 HPLCs, 4 GCs, 2 LC-MS/MS systems, 14 dissolution testers, FTIR, UV-Vis, Karl Fischer, and other equipment and instruments. ncr_translation_input.outcome: Based on the areas inspected, the people met and the documents reviewed, and considering the findings of the inspection, including the observations listed in the Inspection Report, Oxalis Labs, located at Village Theda, P.O. Lodhimajra, Tehsil Baddi, District Solan, Himachal Pradesh, India, was considered to be operating at an acceptable level of compliance with WHO GMP Guidelines. All the non-compliances observed during the inspection that were listed in the full report as well as those reflected in the WHOPIR were addressed by the manufacturer to a satisfactory level, prior to the publication of the WHOPIR This WHOPIR will remain valid for 3 years, provided that the outcome of any inspection conducted during this period is positive.
ncr_translation_input.s1: The quality assurance manual provided the company’s quality policy and quality objectives and outlined the general concepts of QA, as well as the principal components or subsystems of cGMP, which were the joint responsibility of all personnel. It included Hygiene, Validation, Self-inspection, Personnel, Premises, Equipment, Materials, risk analysis, data integrity, technology transfer, and Documentation. The QA was independent of manufacturing operations and reported directly to the corporate QA. …
ncr_translation_input.s10: A corporate SOP provided guidance on imparting training through the Performance Learning Management System (PLMS) and the manual system. The same training procedure was applied to staff and contracted workers.
ncr_translation_input.s11: Appropriate gowning instructions were displayed in the change rooms for the staff and visitors before entering the manufacturing and other areas. 70% IPA was used to sanitize hands. The site-specific procedure was available for personnel hygiene. The personnel working in the manufacturing areas appeared to be gowned as required, including primary, secondary, and over-gowning.
ncr_translation_input.s12: The general block was divided into the Rifa block, the tablet block, and the MDI block. The manufacturer also has an M block for external preparations. WHO products were manufactured in the Rifa and tablet blocks, and the following information was noted: - Rifa block has 2 dispensing booths, 1 sampling booth, 4 granulation, 1 roll compactor, 4 blending, 6 compression machines, 7 coating machines, 2 manual inspection lines, and 5 packing lines (3 blister and 2 strip packing) - Tablet block was equipped with 3 dispensing booths, 3 sampling booths, 4 granulation, 3 blending, 5 compression, 2 coat …
ncr_translation_input.s13: The manufacturing facility was adequately equipped with the instruments and equipment needed to manufacture and test the FPPs. In general, the equipment was maintained adequately. The production equipment was cleaned between batches and product runs, and clean and dirty equipment hold times were established. The status labels on equipment confirmed the last cleaning date and validity.
ncr_translation_input.s14: The inspector visited the warehouse (general tablet), including the sampling, dispensing, quarantine, undertest, approved, and rejected/returned areas. In general, the various storage areas were well-lit, adequately maintained, and clean. The temperature mapping was performed, and hold/cold spots were identified and monitored. The temperature limit of 15-25ºC and relative humidity of NMT 60% were maintained. The environmental management system was implemented in various areas within the warehouse. …
ncr_translation_input.s15: The company used an electronic document management system (DMS) to manage SOPs, specifications, and standard testing procedures. The procedures, specifications, and testing methods reviewed during the inspection appeared to be unambiguous. Responsible personnel prepared, reviewed, and approved the documents. A unique identification number was assigned and traceable across departments. Protocols and reports related to process and cleaning validation were found adequate. …
ncr_translation_input.s16: The inspector visited the non-Rifa (white) section of the site. The site provided separate male/female changerooms and washrooms before entry to the manufacturing areas. Street shoes were removed before entering the primary changeroom, and gowning instructions were displayed on the wall for entry/exit. IPA 70% was used before entering the manufacturing areas. Operators used lockers to store their street clothes. The manufacturing area was divided into ground, first, and second floors. …
ncr_translation_input.s17: The inspector visited the laboratory. The samples were received and stored in the SS cabinet before being assigned to the analysts for analysis. The section head maintained the competency matrix to ensure that trained analysts received the samples. The sample storage area was temperature-monitored using a calibrated thermohygrometer. The laboratory has 218 staff, including 17 microbiologists. The laboratory was equipped with 61 HPLCs (Shimadzu, Agilent, and Thermo Fisher) and 7 GCs using Chromeleon 7.2 software. …
ncr_translation_input.s2: Oxalis Labs manufactures the finished pharmaceutical products for Macleods Pharmaceuticals Limited. The WHO-prequalified and under-assessment FPPs were manufactured in two shared manufacturing areas: the general tablet block and the Rifa block. The change parts, filter bags, sieves, and screens were product-dedicated. Cleaning validation was performed considering solubility, maximum daily dose, PDE values, etc., and the worst case was determined. …
ncr_translation_input.s2_title: Good manufacturing practices for pharmaceutical products
ncr_translation_input.s3: An adequate level of sanitization and hygiene was observed during the inspection of various manufacturing and laboratory areas. The sanitization and hygiene covered personnel, premises, equipment, materials, and other areas.
ncr_translation_input.s4: The Validation Master Plan 2026 for G-Block was reviewed. The plan was prepared annually by the QA team and approved by various department heads. The VMP included personnel responsibilities for executing qualification and validation activities and providing guidance on facility qualification & validation, process validation, cleaning validation, software validation (CSV), utilities validation, analytical method validation, vendor qualification, training, etc. A separate validation master plan for the computerized system was available. …
ncr_translation_input.s5: The SOP for customer complaints was reviewed. The CQA logged all complaints received in Oxalis to TrackWise before further investigation. Macleod's website provided the email addresses and phone numbers of personnel responsible for receiving the complaints. The investigation had to be completed within 5 working days for critical complaints and within 20 to 35 calendar days for major and minor complaints, respectively. Trend analysis was performed quarterly and annually. …
ncr_translation_input.s6: The procedure for product recall from the overseas market was reviewed. The recalls were voluntary and statutory. The recalls were categorized into Class I, II, and III. Mock recalls were conducted annually at the distribution level. From 2023 to December 2025, there were no recalls of WHO prequalified products. In 2026, a voluntary recall was initiated following a complaint from PAHO.
ncr_translation_input.s7: Oxalis Labs is a contract manufacturer for Macleods Pharmaceuticals Limited. The WHO prequalified, and under-assessment products were manufactured on-site, while calibration, qualification, and testing for some tests were carried out at contracted sites.
ncr_translation_input.s7_title: Contract production, analysis and other activities
ncr_translation_input.s8: The self-inspections were conducted following the CQA procedure once every 6-month. A checklist was used to record the areas audited. This section was not inspected in detail.
ncr_translation_input.s8_title: Self-inspection, quality audits and suppliers’ audits and approval

We also propose to provide that the addition of NAC to a dietary supplement is not a prohibited act under section 301(ll) of the FD&C Act.

rows.body: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of additional draft and revised draft product-specific guidances. The draft guidances provide product-specific recommendations on, among other things, the design of bioequivalence (BE) studies to support abbreviated new drug applications (ANDAs). In the Federal Register of June 11, 2010, FDA announced the availability of a guidance for industry titled "Bioequivalence Recommendations for Specific Products" that explained the process that would be used to make product-specific guidances available to the public on FDA's website. The draft guidances identified in this notice were developed using the process described in that guidance.
